Simulate observation data with several types of edge

Source: R/simulations.R
simulate_bison_model_mixture.Rd

Simulates observations of social events in an undirected network of 15 nodes, where each edge belongs to one of several components (types of relationship) with different mean edge weights. Use it to try out bison_mixture(), or to check that it recovers the true number of components.

Usage

simulate_bison_model_mixture(model_type, num_components, component_weights)

Arguments

model_type

Type of data to simulate, "binary" or "count".

num_components

Number of components in the simulation (at least 2).

component_weights

Vector giving the proportion of edges in each component, e.g. c(0.5, 0.5). Must sum to 1.

Value

A list with df_sim, the simulated observations, and df_true, the true edge weights on the link scale. df_sim has columns node_1_id, node_2_id, event and effort (observation effort). It also has a duration column, identical to effort, for code written for earlier versions; new code should use effort.

Details

Component means are evenly spaced between -2.5 and 2.5 on the link scale (log-odds for binary data, log rates for count data), and edge weights within a component have a standard deviation of 0.5. Each dyad is observed between 1 and 20 times, and the data are summed to one row per dyad.

See also

bison_mixture(), simulate_bison_model()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model_mixture(
  "binary", num_components = 2, component_weights = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
head(sim_data$df_sim)
#>   node_1_id node_2_id event effort duration
#> 1         1         2    15     17       17
#> 2         1         3    17     18       18
#> 3         1         4    19     19       19
#> 4         1         5     0     20       20
#> 5         1         6     0      2        2
#> 6         1         7     1     16       16
